verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere is an on-device inference SDK that advertises hardware acceleration ("accelerated by whatever silicon the device has", Hexagon NPU on Snapdragon), so diagnosing acceleration fallback is a fair axis for it. However, nothing in the evidence documents diagnostic output, logs, or events explaining why GPU/NPU acceleration failed or that execution fell back to CPU. The one mention of fallback (M1/M2 falling back to llama.cpp) is a compatibility note, not a diagnostic. The 'no silent move' claim concerns hosted vs local execution, not GPU vs CPU.
